The petitioner, who was arrested on 23.05.2024 and remanded to judicial custody on 24.05.2024 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 r/w 120 B of IPC in Crime No.88 of 2024, on the file https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of the respondent police seeks bail.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the litigation is on land and the Hennur Project between the de-facto complainant and his brother, at this juncture the de-facto complainant wanted to withdraw his investment along with the investment made by his brother and after the dispute arose, there was an Memorandum of Understanding (hereinafter referred as MOU) dated 22.03.2023 executed Mr.Vivek Jairaj vs The State Rep.

The matter was referred to arbitrator.
Hence, the complaint.
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is an innocent person and has not committed any such offence as alleged by the prosecution.
He further submits that in order to arrest the petitioner, a false complaint has been given against him as if he entered into MOU with the de-facto complainant and cheated him.
He further submitted that the petitioner has been in jail from 23.05.2024.
Therefore, he prayed to grant bail to the petitioner.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.

Learned counsel for the de-facto complainant/Intervenor raised objections stating that as per the MOU executed by the petitioner dated 22.03.2023, he also agreed to pay a sum of Rs.2,50,00,000/-
to the de- facto complainant but he failed to pay the amount and the dishonoured cheques issued by the petitioner clearly shows that he wants to cheat and de-fraud the de-facto complainant.
Hence he raised strong objection in granting bail to the petitioner.
5. The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) appearing for the respondent submits that the petitioner had cheated the de-facto complainant to the tune of Rs.2,50,00,000/-.
He vehemently opposes for granting of bail to the petitioner.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the petitioner/A2 has been complied with the conditional order dated 18.06.2024 by depositing Rs.75,00,000/- and therefore, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the petitioner with certain conditions.
